I. GENERAL
The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) Protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) developing the intellectual life of the nation and (4) participating in the implementation of world order based on (a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. To achieve these objectives, in accordance with the doctrine of trias politica, there are three State powers namely Executive, Legislative, and Judiciary. In Indonesia these three powers complement each other, for the implementation of clean and authoritative governance from the national level to the regional level.
The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of power, carried out by both men and women, are also regulated by law.
The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.
Regional autonomy that is implemented has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (regional regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to serve as a guideline for regional governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and Other Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in their respective regions.
The Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is based on Pancasila, and based on the 1945 Constitution, and refers to many Laws especially those regulating the protection of women and children victims of violence, including Law No. 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, Law no. 39 of 1999 Concerning Human Rights, Law No. 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law no. 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law No. 23 of 2002 Concerning Child Protection, and other related Laws.
With the provisions of the Laws above, we can understand how great the attention of the Central Government is to protect its citizens who are in an unpleasant position, namely when becoming victims of violence, however in reality legal processes are still rarely carried out for victims of violence which nowadays are increasingly numerous and complex in their problems. And in South Bangka very few existing problems can be resolved legally due to ignorance of the community and the absence of specific legal regulations that become legal regulations that can be used in the region.
It is hoped that with the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, in South Bangka Regency in particular, handling and rehabilitation as well as reunification can be carried out properly, and the process of preventing violence against women and children becomes smoother, so that there will be less and eventually no more violence against Women and Children.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Bangka Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of South Bangka.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Bangka Regency as an element of regional government administration.
5. Principle of Respect and Recognition of Human Rights and Dignity is based on Respect for the rights of victims, Justice and gender equality, Non-Discrimination and the best interests of victims.
6. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psychological and legal services.
7. Social Community Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
11. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
12. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
13. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
14. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
15. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
16. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
17. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
18. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
19. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
20. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various interrelated parts, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
21. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of violence from the Region to the Region of Origin.
1.2.rationale: The policy explicitly defines sexual violence as a form of violence, including examples such as sexual harassment and forced sexual intercourse.
